summary_html: Youth remains in **extended foster care** or receives **transitional services** after age 18 under federal programs promoting independence.
authority_html:
- **Chafee Foster Care Independence Act (CFCIA)** — independent-living and transition funding  
- **FCSIAA** — extends care to age 21 with education and housing supports

primary_citations.citation_text: California - Penal Code §§ 11164–11174.3 (CANRA – Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act)
California - Welfare & Institutions Code § 300 et seq. (Juvenile dependency proceedings)

regulations_applicable.title: Title 22 - Social Security (DSS Child Welfare Regulations)
Title 11 - Law (DOJ Child Abuse Central Index)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the juvenile court erred in terminating dependency jurisdiction over a nonminor dependent because the order rested on a misunderstanding of the law governing extended foster care eligibility and acceptable supervised independent living placements.
key_cases.relevance: Directly governs termination of juvenile court jurisdiction over a nonminor dependent in California's extended foster care program.
key_cases.quote: We agree the court erred because it based its order on a misunderstanding of the law.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the probate court applied an incorrect legal framework in denying special immigrant juvenile predicate findings, and that a young person's uncontradicted declaration can alone support findings of parental abuse, neglect or abandonment and that return to the home country is not in the child's best interest.
key_cases.relevance: Controls SIJ predicate findings for older youth, including nonminors, who need them to stabilize status as they transition out of care.
key_cases.quote: We conclude the probate court applied an incorrect legal framework in ruling on Saul's petition.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that the case plan and case records provisions of the federal Child Welfare Act, 42 U.S.C. sections 671(a)(16) and 675(1), create rights enforceable by foster children under section 1983, while the guardian ad litem provision does not, and reinstated the children's substantive due process claims arising from harm suffered in state custody.
key_cases.relevance: Makes the case plan and records duties that govern a youth's transition out of care judicially enforceable.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the case plan provisions of the CWA, codified at §§ 671(a)(16) and 675(1), are enforceable through § 1983.

state_agency.name: California Department of Social Services
state_agency.hotline: No statewide number. Call your county's 24-hour hotline

extended_foster_care_age: Up to age 21 (nonminor dependents; Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 11403)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
